q: Microsoft Office is classified as which type of software and licence?
explain: Office is application software and is proprietary (closed source).

q: In which year did Bill Gates announce the Office suite?
explain: The suite was announced in 1988; the first release (for Mac) followed in 1989 and Windows in 1990.

q: The first commercial Microsoft Office package appeared for which platform?
explain: The first commercial Office package was for Apple Macintosh in 1989; Office for Windows came in 1990.

q: Which three applications formed the core of the original Microsoft Office package?
explain: The original core applications were Word, Excel and PowerPoint; Outlook and Paint were not in it.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised Microsoft Office release?
explain: Windows Vista was an operating system; there was no Office Vista edition.

q: Which statement about Office editions is correct?
options: Office 2021 was the final Office release
Office 2019 and 2021 were one-time purchase editions
explain: Office 2019 and 2021 were perpetual (one-time purchase) editions; Office 2024 followed Office 2021 and Mac 2011 was real.

q: Which Microsoft Office application is a desktop relational database management system?
explain: Access stores records in tables, links them with relationships and retrieves data with queries.

q: Which application is used for email together with managing contacts, calendars and appointments?
explain: Outlook handles email and personal information management.

q: Which Office application is mainly used to record and organise digital notes and ideas?
explain: OneNote is the note-taking application; Publisher is for desktop publishing.

q: Which Office application is designed for newsletters, flyers, business cards and greeting cards?
explain: Publisher is a desktop-publishing tool, now retired from Microsoft 365 in October 2026.

q: Picture Manager replaced which earlier tool in Office 2003?
explain: Picture Manager replaced Photo Editor in Office 2003; it was a replacement, not simply a renaming.

q: What does MOS stand for in the context of Microsoft certification?
explain: MOS means Microsoft Office Specialist, a certification of practical Office skills.

q: Which of the following was NOT an original component of Microsoft Office?
explain: Paint is a Windows drawing application and was never an original Office component.

q: On which date did Office 365 have its commercial launch?
explain: Office 365 launched commercially on 28 June 2011, after announcement and early testing in 2010.

q: Several Office 365 subscriptions adopted Microsoft 365 names on which date?
explain: The plan renaming took place on 21 April 2020, though some Office 365 plan names remained.

q: In which year did Microsoft introduce the Microsoft 365 brand for business offerings?
explain: The Microsoft 365 business brand arrived in 2017, bundling Office 365, Windows and enterprise security services.

q: How many people can use a Microsoft 365 Family plan, including the owner?
explain: The Family plan covers up to six people in total, including the subscription owner; Personal is for one person.

q: Which statement about Microsoft 365 is correct?
options: It is online-only and has no desktop apps
It works only on Windows PCs
Eligible plans include desktop apps that can work offline
Every plan includes every desktop application
explain: Microsoft 365 combines cloud services with installed apps that can work offline; apps vary by plan.

q: Which Microsoft 365 service is commonly used to hold shared team content, with organisational sites and document libraries?
explain: SharePoint provides shared sites and libraries; OneDrive usually holds an individual's files.

q: Which Microsoft tool is used for chats, online meetings and video conferencing?
explain: Microsoft Teams is the collaboration and meeting tool; the correct name is Teams, not Team.

q: Which Microsoft product is a business analytics platform for interactive reports and dashboards?
explain: Power BI connects to data to build interactive reports and dashboards, and is not automatically included in every Microsoft 365 plan.

q: Which feature gives AI assistance inside supported Microsoft applications?
explain: Copilot is the AI assistant; its availability and limits depend on the plan.

q: Office 2024 is sold as which type of licence?
explain: Office 2024 is a one-time purchase, unlike Microsoft 365, which is a subscription.

q: On what date did consumer editions of Office 2024 become available?
explain: Consumer Office 2024 editions became available on 1 October 2024.

q: Which Office 2024 edition adds Outlook and commercial-use rights to Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote?
explain: Home & Business 2024 adds Outlook and commercial use rights; Home covers Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote for one PC or Mac.

q: Which PowerPoint feature lets you place a live camera feed directly on a slide?
explain: Cameo places a live camera object on a slide, and styles and effects can be applied to it.

q: When does support for Office 2024 end?
explain: Office 2024 support ends in October 2029; Office 2021 support ended in October 2026.

q: What is the LibreOffice equivalent of Microsoft Excel?
explain: Calc is the LibreOffice spreadsheet program; Writer is word processing and Impress is presentations.

q: Which of the following is Apple's presentation application?
explain: Apple's presentation app is Keynote; Slides is Google's and Impress is LibreOffice's.

q: Which LibreOffice component is used for vector graphics, diagrams and flowcharts?
explain: Draw handles vector graphics and flowcharts; Base is for databases and Math is for formulas.

q: Which organisation supports the development of LibreOffice, a free and open-source suite?
explain: LibreOffice is built by a worldwide community supported by The Document Foundation, a nonprofit.

q: Word was initially known by which name?
explain: Microsoft Word began as Multi-Tool Word; early release history dates to 1983.

q: Which two people played central roles in developing Microsoft Word?
explain: Charles Simonyi and Richard Brodie were central to Word's development at Microsoft; Brodie wrote much of the original program.

q: In which year did Microsoft acquire LinkedIn, a professional networking platform?
explain: Microsoft acquired LinkedIn in 2016; the acquisition was completed on 8 December 2016.
